svg.title: a freshly generated project passes its own quality gate: OSV checks dependencies where their owner can fix them
svg.text: a freshly generated project passes its own quality gate
Scenario: OSV checks dependencies where their owner can fix them
The toolbox answers for its own tools
The project answers for its own dependencies
Without vulnerable dependencies of its own, the project passes

g.text: Given every framework tool in a generated project contains the same vulnerable package
GitLab shows lodash 4.17.20, a version with a known vulnerability, in the CodeceptJS lockfile the project inherits from
the toolbox. Every framework tool under .config gets the same vulnerable lockfile.
Then the toolbox's OSV scan reports the same vulnerable framework tools
The same project, scanned once with the toolbox's own scanner configuration: the scanner's command, printed first,
leaves no .config folder out. GitLab's code:megalinter job fails.
OSV reads every framework tool and lists each lockfile with lodash 4.17.20 and advisory GHSA-35jh-r3h4-6jhm. The toolbox
catches the tools it ships.
When the developer adds vulnerable dependencies in project-owned locations
GitLab's page for the commit "test: add project dependencies". Its Files list shows four new lockfiles, each with lodash
4.17.20: one at the root, one under application/.config, and two in .config folders the project created itself,
codeceptjs-extra and project-tool.
And the developer updates the framework through Copier
GitLab's page for the Copier update commit. It changes two files: .copier-answers.yml moves from 1.0.0 to 1.0.1, and
.config/jq/Taskfile.yml is the one marker file the test release 1.0.1 adds.
The project's scanner settings and its four lockfiles are not in the commit: the update leaves them alone.
Then OSV reports every project-owned copy of the vulnerable package
After the update, the project's code:megalinter job fails. The scanner's command still leaves the framework tools out,
with --experimental-exclude=.config/ansible, .config/codeceptjs and the others.
OSV reads only the four lockfiles the project owns, .config/project-tool included, and reports lodash 4.17.20 and
advisory GHSA-35jh-r3h4-6jhm in each one.
When the developer removes the vulnerable dependencies from the project's own locations
GitLab's page for the commit "test: remove project dependencies": the four project lockfiles are deleted. The framework
tools keep their vulnerable lockfiles.
Then the project's OSV scan leaves the framework tools to the toolbox and passes
The same job now passes. OSV still leaves the framework tools out, says "No package sources found" for the project, then
"No issues found". MegaLinter ends on "Successfully linted all files without errors" and GitLab marks the job Passed.
The framework tools are still vulnerable: as the first chapter showed, that is the toolbox's job.
